battle.name: 敘利亞-以法蓮戰爭
battle.brief: 公元前七三六年起，亞蘭王利新與北以色列王比加圍困耶路撒冷，亞哈斯以殿中金銀向亞述求援，提革拉毗列三世西征：破大馬士革、殺利新、奪基列與拿弗他利、平定加薩，猶大自此淪為亞述屬國。卡面的埃及月牙劍是青銅時代舊物，到本役已失傳數百年，戰場上是鐵矛、短劍、弓矢、車兵與撞槌攻城塔。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 這場戰爭是前八世紀中葉黎凡特三方聯手與亞述帝國的一次直接較量，捲入五方勢力。亞蘭即大馬士革王國，國王利新是亞蘭王朝的末代君主，都城大馬士革控制安達黎斯山東麓與約旦河東的商路，軍隊以步兵與弓手為主，倚靠城牆、渡口與基列一帶的縱深。北方以色列即撒馬利亞王國，國王比加以侍從身分殺死前任君主比迦利亞奪位，拒絕再向亞述繳納進貢；其守軍集中在加利利與基列北境，兵員有限而地勢險要。猶大即耶路撒冷王國，國王亞哈斯是少年即位的君主，軍力薄弱，被亞蘭與以色列聯軍圍困在耶路撒冷，只能求援於亞述。第四方是亞述帝國，國王提革拉毗列三世在位於前七四五年至前七二七年，剛完成對安納托利亞的兼併，軍隊由步兵、弓兵、車兵與騎兵組成，並大量使用被擄民充當的戰俘步兵，工匠分隊隨軍備有撞槌與攻城塔。非利士諸城以加薩為主，站在埃及一方支援猶大的敵人，埃及法老則以使節與援助維持對加薩的影響；約旦河東一帶由「古爾的阿拉伯人」控制，其首領在基列方向與亞述周旋，聯軍的北方翼線正壓在這一帶。
countriesEn: This war was a direct collision between a three-sided coalition in the Levant and the Neo-Assyrian Empire in the middle of the eighth century BC, and it drew five parties into it. Aram, the kingdom of Damascus, was ruled by Rezin, the last king of the Aramean dynasty; the capital commanded the routes of the Anti-Lebanon foothills and the east bank of the Jordan, and its army was built on infantry and archers, resting on city walls, fords and the depth of Gilead behind them. Israel to the north, the kingdom of Samaria, was ruled by Pekah, who had killed his predecessor Pekahiah while serving him and seized the throne; he refused to pay the Assyrian tribute any longer, and his defenders were concentrated in Galilee and northern Gilead, few in number but on difficult ground. Judah, the kingdom of Jerusalem, was ruled by the young king Ahaz; his military strength was thin, he was shut up in Jerusalem by the coalition of Aram and Israel, and the only course left open to him was to seek Assyrian help. The fourth party was Assyria itself, ruled by Tiglath-pileser III, who reigned from 745 to 727 BC and had just completed the annexation of Anatolia; his army combined infantry, archers, chariot troops and cavalry and made heavy use of foreign prisoners enrolled as infantry, with engineer detachments, battering rams and siege towers travelling in train. The Philistine cities, Gaza chief among them, stood on the Egyptian side against Judah's enemies, while the Egyptian pharaoh kept his grip on Gaza by envoys and aid; the country east of the Jordan was held by the 'Arab of Gur', whose ruler manoeuvred against Assyry in the Gilead direction, and the northern flank of the coalition was pressed exactly along that line.
people: 決定這場戰爭走向的是亞述王提革拉毗列三世。亞哈斯遣使帶著金銀與殿中器皿前往大馬士革求援，亞述王便以此為口實揮師西進，把一次王朝危機變成自己的征服。猶大王亞哈斯的角色被動而關鍵：他面對亞蘭王利新與以色列王比加的聯軍逼近都城，非利士人攻陷伯斐（迦特），以東人掠奪猶大南境，國軍被圍在耶路撒冷城內；他選擇交出重寶求饒，並按亞述王在大馬士革所見的壇樣，在耶路撒冷聖殿另建新祭壇，此舉在後世被記為猶大宗教史最黑暗的一段。亞蘭王利新在圍城失利後回援大馬士革，城破之日被殺，亞蘭國從此不復存在。以色列王比加拒納進貢，戰敗被殺，位子由侍從何細奪取；何細隨即與亞述絕盟，前七三二年被亞述擒獲。耶路撒冷先知以賽亞是另一個關鍵人物：他在亞哈斯面前斥責聯軍為兩根冒煙的柴，勸國王不要靠人手而要仰望，並預言亞述將親自圍困耶路撒冷、以馬內利之記號將要顯現；亞哈斯沒有採納他的話，同期的彌迦則宣告車兵必被剪除，兩位先知在亂局中各守一端。
peopleEn: What decided the course of this war was Tiglath-pileser III of Assyria. Ahaz sent envoys to Damascus carrying the silver and gold of the temple, and the Assyrian king took that submission as his pretext and marched west, turning a dynastic crisis into a conquest of his own. Ahaz of Judah was passive yet decisive: with the coalition of Rezin of Aram and Pekah of Israel closing on his capital, the Philistines taking Gath and the Edomites raiding the southern approaches of Judah, the army of the state was shut up inside Jerusalem; he gave up heavy treasure to buy mercy, and, having seen in Damascus the pattern of the altar in the Assyrian court, had a new altar of that design built in the temple at Jerusalem, an act that later tradition marked as the darkest episode in the religious history of Judah. Rezin of Aram, once the siege had gone wrong, fell back to defend Damascus and was killed on the day the city fell; the Aramean state ceased to exist from then on. Pekah of Israel, having refused tribute, was killed after his defeat, and his place was taken by his officer Hoshea, who immediately broke with Assyria and was taken prisoner by the Assyrians in 732 BC. Isaiah of Jerusalem was another key figure: he called the coalition two smoking stumps, urged the king to rely on something above human helpers, and prophesied that Assyria itself would besiege Jerusalem and that the sign of Immanuel would be given; Ahaz did not take his counsel, and his contemporary Micah proclaimed that the chariots would be cut off, the two prophets holding opposite ends of the crisis.
kits: 卡面這件埃及月牙劍是青銅時代的工藝：外彎的單刃，刃口內彎，砍進之後不必把劍拔出來再劈；新王國時期它是步兵的近身砍劈兵器，通常與盾牌並用，也見於王室肖像與神廟浮雕。這種兵器在公元前十二世紀青銅時代晚期之後逐漸退出軍用，最晚一批實物見於第二十一王朝前後的墓葬，到本役開打時已經失傳數百年，是一件年代不合的展示古物，並未出現在黎凡特的任何一座城牆下。當時真正在場的，是亞述一系的鐵矛頭短劍與斧、複合弓配鐵或骨箭鏃、柳條編織的方盾、魚鱗式鎧甲與帶護頗的頭盔，以及雙馬或單馬的輕型戰車；攻城裝備包括撞槌、可移動的攻城塔、填壕的工兵與掘壕分隊。猶大與以色列方面的冷兵器是鐵短劍與鐵矛，以弓手為主力，鄰近地區以投石著稱，戰車仍然存在但數量有限，非利士人素以鐵車見稱。耶路撒冷城防靠城牆、望樓、外濠與示劍泉的水源，城內另設蓄水池與引水渠。若要找結構上的對應，月牙劍的邏輯是「以盾護身、以單刃一次斬落解決目標」，這與前八世紀步兵「以長矛與弓矢先削弱敵陣、短兵只在盾後完成最後擊殺」的分工同屬一種思路，只是材料與工藝已經換代：銅刃面對前八世紀常見的鐵甲與鐵盾，早已不堪一擊。
kitsEn: The Egyptian khopesh on the card is a piece of Bronze Age craftwork: a single-edged blade whose edge curves inward, so that once it has bitten it does not have to be drawn back for the next blow; in the New Kingdom it was the close-quarter chopping weapon of the infantry, carried together with a shield, and it appears in royal portraits and in temple reliefs. The type fell out of military use gradually after the Late Bronze Age, around the twelfth century BC, and the latest specimens come from burials of roughly the Twenty-first Dynasty, so several centuries before this war it had already disappeared: it is an anachronistic display piece, and it was present on no rampart in the Levant. What was actually on the field was the Assyrian armoury of iron-tipped spears, short swords and axes, composite bows with iron or bone arrowheads, tall wicker shields, scale corslets and helmets with cheek pieces, and light chariots drawn by two horses or one; the siege train included battering rams, movable siege towers, sappers for filling the ditch and parties sent to dig under the walls. Judah and Israel fought with iron short swords and iron spears, relied chiefly on archers, were famous for the sling in the neighbouring highlands, and possessed chariots in limited numbers, the Philistines being long celebrated for their iron ones. The defences of Jerusalem rested on the wall, its towers, an outer ditch and the spring of Gihon, with a reservoir and channels inside the city. If a structural counterpart is wanted, the logic of the khopesh is that the shield protects the body and one downward cut ends the matter; that is the same division of labour as the infantry of the eighth century BC, where spears and arrows weaken the enemy line first and short weapons deliver the last killing behind the shield, only the material and the craft had changed hands: a copper edge facing the iron armour and iron shields common by then was never going to do.
tactics: 聯軍的企圖是兩面作戰：利新從北方拿下基列與「古爾的阿拉伯人」之地，切斷以色列通往亞述與北方商路的咽喉，同時把戰線壓到約旦河東；比加則取伯斐、封住猶大西境，切斷亞哈斯與沿海平原及通往亞述的沿海道路；兩軍合兵直指耶路撒冷，先滅亞蘭與以法蓮兩家，再合力收拾猶大。聯軍的失誤是沒有算到亞述的介入速度，而亞述的戰術正是以速度取勝：第一段直撲大馬士革，切斷利新的外援，聯盟因缺血而瓦解；第二段處理撒馬利亞與基列，扶植傀儡何細；第三段西征平定加薩的叛亂，收受亞哈斯的進貢，把以拉割給以東，重新劃定猶大的疆界。亞述的攻城術是本役最吃重的部分：撞槌撞擊牆基、攻城塔靠近後以弓手掩護登城、工兵填壕與掘壕分隊、封鎖水源；亞述軍隊南下時曾圍攻利比拿，而耶路撒冷的供水是守城關鍵，先知書與史家都提到圍城者必須處理城內的水源。亞哈斯一方的應對是加固城防、遣使進貢求援，並在亞述使者到來時以大馬士革的壇樣取代原有祭制。結局是聯軍各自崩潰：利新回援大馬士革，北以色列被孤立，比加被自己人殺掉。
tacticsEn: The plan of the coalition was to operate on two fronts at once. Rezin took Gilead and the country of the 'Arab of Gur' from the north, cutting off Israel's throat toward Assyria and the northern caravan roads while pushing the line east of the Jordan; Pekah took Gath, sealed the western side of Judah and cut Ahaz off from the coastal plain and from the coast road to Assyria; the two armies then joined and moved straight on Jerusalem, with the intention of destroying Aram and Ephraim first and dealing with Judah afterwards. The coalition's mistake was in not reckoning with the speed of the Assyrian intervention, and speed was precisely what Assyrian tactics turned on. The first stage struck straight at Damascus, cutting Rezin off from his allies, and the alliance came apart for want of blood. The second stage dealt with Samaria and Gilead and installed a puppet in the shape of Hoshea. The third stage marched west, put down the revolt of Gaza, took Ahaz's tribute, cut Elath away from Judah and gave it to Edom, and redrew the frontier of Judah. The siegecraft of Assyria was the weightiest part of the campaign: rams beating against the base of a wall, siege towers brought up under cover of archers, engineers filling the ditch and parties digging under the defences, and the sealing of the water supply; the Assyrian columns besieged Libnah on their way south, and the water of Jerusalem was the crux of the defence, both the prophetic books and the chronicles dwelling on what the besieger had to do with the city's water. Ahaz's side answered by strengthening the fortifications, sending envoys with tribute to ask for help, and, when the Assyrian emissary arrived, replacing the older cult with an altar built to the Damascus pattern. The coalition came apart at the end: Rezin fell back to Damascus, northern Israel was isolated, and Pekah was killed by his own men.
data: 可據以書寫的數字大致如下。時間上，本役自前七三六年起（部分史家定於前七三五年），至前七三二年亞述平定加薩、重新劃定邊界而收束，前後約三至四年；提革拉毗列三世在位於前七四五年至前七二七年，亞哈斯在位十六年，約前七四○年至前七二四年，比加在位二十年，何細在位九年。進貢數字可作實力量度：比加的前任以色列王一次向亞述交付一千他連得銀子、一百他連得金子，另加十他連得金器、十他連得銀器、十二頭牛、一千頭羊、一千隻山羊、二千頭牛、二千隻羊、一千匹騾子、一千匹母駱駝與一千匹公駱駝；亞哈斯送出的則是殿中金銀器皿與國庫珍寶。距離上，大馬士革到耶路撒冷約二百四十公里，伯斐到耶路撒冷約六十餘公里，基列到亞述前線則在千里上下，亞述軍隊在黎凡特境內的實際行程以數百公里計。人口流動有明確記載：基列與拿弗他利的居民被擄往亞述，加薩的居民被遷往撒馬利亞，大馬士革部分居民亦遭擄徙。傷亡與兵員編制則無可靠數字：兩部史書都沒有留下可核的損失記載，本役相關的亞述年銘也只存殘片，過程多靠《列王紀》與《歷代志》重建。作戰月份史無明載，亞述的遠征多在秋收後出發，卡面取九月。
dataEn: The figures that can be given on good authority are roughly these. In time, the war began in 736 BC (some historians place the outbreak in 735 BC) and closed in 732 BC, when Assyria pacified Gaza and redefined the frontier, a matter of some three to four years in all; Tiglath-pileser III reigned from 745 to 727 BC, Ahaz reigned sixteen years, roughly from 740 to 724 BC, Pekah reigned twenty years and Hoshea nine. The tribute figures give a measure of the two sides: the king of Israel before Pekah paid Assyria in a single payment a thousand talents of silver and a hundred talents of gold, together with ten talents of golden vessels and ten of silver vessels, twelve oxen, a thousand head of sheep, a thousand goats, two thousand oxen, two thousand sheep, a thousand mules, a thousand female camels and a thousand male camels; what Ahaz sent was the silver and gold of the temple and the treasure of the treasury. As for distance, Damascus to Jerusalem is about two hundred and forty kilometres, Gath to Jerusalem a little over sixty, and Gilead to the Assyrian frontier something like a thousand, so that the Assyrian columns covered several hundred kilometres inside the Levant. The movement of population is explicitly recorded: the inhabitants of Gilead and Naphtali were deported to Assyria, those of Gaza were resettled in Samaria, and part of the population of Damascus was carried off as well. Casualties and order of battle are not known on any reliable authority: neither chronicle leaves a verifiable account of the losses, and the Assyrian annal relating to this war survives only in fragments, so the course of the campaign is reconstructed from Kings and Chronicles. The month of the fighting is nowhere stated; Assyrian expeditions normally set out after the harvest, and the card takes September.
cause: 這場戰爭的直接起因，是亞述宗主體系的一次鬆動。以色列與亞蘭長期向亞述進貢，比加的前任曾一次交付一千他連得銀子與一百他連得金子；比加殺死比迦利亞奪位之後停納進貢，亞述施加壓力，亞蘭王利新則乘勢向北方擴張，奪取以色列的基列與「古爾的阿拉伯人」之地，把自己的勢力伸進約旦河東，兩邊的衝突於是同時爆發。壓到猶大身上的是恐懼：亞哈斯登位不久，亞蘭與以色列兩家同時反叛，聯軍打著推翻亞哈斯的名號逼近耶路撒冷，非利士人攻下伯斐，以東人趁勢劫掠南境，國軍被圍在城內。以賽亞在城門口說國王的心與百姓的心一同煙霧瀰瀰，勸他不要因人手而恐懼，先知並把這場危機解讀成對猶大王室的審判，亞哈斯卻把安全押在亞述身上，寧可繳出重寶換取亞述出兵，免得城破。以賽亞書七章十七至二十節更預見亞述將親自圍困耶路撒冷，於是先知看到的不是拯救，而是又一次被審判的來臨；這也說明，在當時的耶路撒冷，人心早已在聯盟、進貢與盟約信用之間反覆權衡。
causeEn: The immediate cause of this war was a loosening in the Assyrian system of lordship. Israel and Aram had long paid tribute to Assyria, and the king of Israel before Pekah had delivered a thousand talents of silver and a hundred talents of gold in a single payment; when Pekah killed Pekahiah and took the throne he stopped paying, and Assyria began to apply pressure. Rezin of Aram took the opportunity to expand northward, taking Gilead and the country of the 'Arab of Gur' from Israel and pushing his own reach east of the Jordan, so that the two conflicts broke out at the same time. What was pressed on Judah was fear. Ahaz had not long been on the throne when Aram and Israel revolted together, the coalition advanced on Jerusalem under the banner of destroying Ahaz, the Philistines took Gath, the Edomites raided the southern approaches, and the army of the state was shut up inside the city. Isaiah at the gate said that the heart of the king and the heart of the people were both clouded with smoke, and urged him not to be afraid of human helpers; the prophet read the crisis as a judgement on the house of David, but Ahaz put his safety in Assyrian hands, preferring to hand over heavy treasure and buy Assyrian intervention rather than see the city taken. Isaiah 7:17-20 goes further and foresees Assyria itself besieging Jerusalem, so what the prophet saw was not deliverance but the coming of a second judgement. It also shows that in Jerusalem of that moment the question of allegiance was being weighed again and again between alliance, tribute and the credit of oaths.
impact: 這場戰爭之後，黎凡特北部的權力版圖被重新畫了一遍。亞蘭王國消亡，大馬士革降為亞述的邊疆行省，亞蘭人被分批擄往撒馬利亞等地；大馬士革從此數百年留在亞述及其後繼者的版圖上，成為日後敘利亞一名所指的中心地。以色列失去基列與拿弗他利，被擄民安置，比加死、何細成傀儡王，撒馬利亞的覆亡已無可挽回，十年後（前七二二年）北方王國終於滅亡。猶大保住卻付出了代價：亞哈斯割讓以拉與南境，沿海的伯斐落入非利士人之手，國土向內收縮，成為亞述的附庸，直到希西家在亞述王辛那赫布晚年才敢挑戰亞述，前七○四年辛那赫布死於軍中。制度上，亞述在此地建立總督、稅收與分區安置被擄民的行省體制，黎凡特的族群分布因此重塑，日後撒馬利亞一帶出現的數族被擄民，正是同一套辦法的延續。亞哈斯在聖殿另建大馬士革式祭壇、廢除舊有器物的做法，成為猶大宗教史上最黑暗的一段，後來由其子希西家全面推翻，兩代人的更替也因此格外刺眼。
impactEn: After this war the political map of the northern Levant was redrawn. The Aramean state disappeared; Damascus became a frontier province of Assyria and Arameans were deported in batches to Samaria and elsewhere; Damascus remained for the next several centuries inside the empire of Assyria and its successors, and became the central place to which the later name of Syria would attach. Israel lost Gilead and Naphtali, received a settled population of deportees, lost Pekah and was ruled by a puppet in the person of Hoshea; the fall of Samaria was already beyond repair, and ten years later, in 722 BC, the northern kingdom was destroyed at last. Judah survived at a price: Ahaz surrendered Elath and the southern approaches, Gath on the coast passed to the Philistines, the territory contracted inward and the state became an Assyrian vassal, not daring to challenge Assyria until the closing years of Sennacherib, who died in his own camp in 704 BC. Institutionally, Assyria set up here a provincial system of governors, taxation and the settlement of deported populations, and the ethnic composition of the Levant was reshaped; the peoples later settled around Samaria were the continuation of the same procedure. Ahaz's building of a Damascus-style altar in the temple and the removal of the older cult became the darkest chapter in the religious history of Judah, and his son Hezekiah later reversed it entirely, which makes the change of generation especially stark.
result: 結果是聯軍徹底失敗，而猶大以屈服換取存續。利新回援大馬士革後城破被殺，亞蘭國從此在名冊上消失；北以色列被切斷外援，比加被部下所殺，何細被扶立卻隨即與亞述決裂，前七三二年被擒；加薩的叛亂被平定，居住者被遷往撒馬利亞；亞哈斯送出殿中金銀、割地於以東，只換得耶路撒冷不被攻破與亞述暫時不加兵。主流的解釋是亞述的西進迫使聯軍在耶路撒冷解圍，各自趕回自己的防線；至於圍城最終如何收場，兩部史書的記載並不完全一致：《列王紀》說亞哈斯以進貢換得耶路撒冷保全，《歷代志》卻記他被押往大馬士革，而以賽亞書七章十七至二十節所預言的亞述親征耶路撒冷是否應驗，至今仍有爭論。整體而言，聯盟、進貢與盟約信用決定了這場戰爭的勝負，而不是任何單件兵器的鋒刃；卡面的月牙劍在亞述的撞槌與攻城塔面前既無從發揮，也未曾出現在這片土地，這正是青銅時代的砍劈兵器與前八世紀的圍城與外交之間的一道分界。
resultEn: The coalition failed completely, and Judah survived by submission. Rezin fell back to Damascus, the city was taken and he was killed, and Aram vanished from the roll of states; northern Israel was cut off from its ally, Pekah was killed by his own men, Hoshea was set up only to break with Assyria and was taken prisoner in 732 BC; the revolt of Gaza was put down and its people resettled in Samaria; Ahaz gave up the silver and gold of the temple and a strip of land to Edom, and received in exchange that Jerusalem would not be taken and that Assyria would not press the siege for the moment. The prevailing explanation is that the Assyrian march to the west forced the coalition to lift the siege of Jerusalem and each party to hurry back to its own front; the closing of the siege itself is not told identically in the two chronicles: Kings says that Ahaz bought the safety of Jerusalem with tribute, while Chronicles says he was carried in chains to Damascus, and whether the Assyrian invasion of Jerusalem foreseen in Isaiah 7:17-20 was fulfilled is still argued. As a whole it was alliances, tribute and the keeping of oaths that decided this war, not the edge of any single weapon. The khopesh on the card could have had no part against Assyrian rams and siege towers, and it was never present in that country; it stands as the line between the chopping blades of the Bronze Age and the siegecraft and diplomacy of the eighth century BC.
